text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Candidates for the June parliamentary elections intensify campaigning.
- Retired association officials say a newly adopted law cutting employee retirement limit threatens a retirement fund.
- Security forces kill 28 "terrorists" in the recent past days in the western provinces of Tissemsilt and Saida.
- The authorities allow pharmacies to open for sale during the night.
- Socialist Forces Front's leader Ali Rachedi sharpens his poll campaign rhetoric saying pro-government militias are "terrorists".
- The government sponsors a workshop over build, offer and transfer (BOT) infrastructures' financing formula in the aim to lure private sector into financing part of Algeria's infrastructure.
- Election watchdog warns the National Democratic Rally (RND), grouping government supporters, and its rival Islamist-leaning Movement for a Peaceful Society over campaign postings.
